cur:catacombs-sarcophagus-31532.summary: Two registers of biblical scenes surround a shell medallion holding the portraits of a couple. Christ appears repeatedly as miracle-worker among the apostles, alongside Old Testament scenes and episodes from the life of Peter.
facts: Commons notes restorations by the 18th-century sculptor-restorer Bartolomeo Cavaceppi.
It belongs to the double-register type with a central clipeus, like the Dogmatic Sarcophagus in the same museum.
cur:catacombs-sarcophagus-31532.notes: Individual scenes have not been verified one by one; parts are 18th-century restoration.

cur:manuscripts-st-emmeram-adoration-of-.summary: High in a starry heaven, the Lamb stands in a medallion holding a cross-staff, while the twenty-four elders, seated in two great curving rows, rise and lift their golden crowns toward him. A star shines in the blue vault between them, and half-naked personifications recline in the lower corners. The page is a sumptuous vision of the heavenly liturgy offered to Christ the Lamb.
facts: The Codex Aureus of St Emmeram was produced for Charles the Bald in 870; its jewelled gold cover is among the very few treasure bindings of that date to survive.
Charles gave the book to Arnulf of Carinthia, who donated it to St Emmeram's Abbey in Regensburg, where it remained for most of its history.

links.label: Wikipedia: Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram

cur:manuscripts-st-emmeram-adoration-of-.notes: Christ is represented symbolically as the Lamb. Folio usually cited as 6r; another Commons scan labels it 'fol. 15'.

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: At the left, the haloed Christ stands before a seated accuser and soldiers; at the right, beside a building, Peter sits by a fire with a servant-girl while a cock crows on top of a column. The verse above reads 'I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth'.
facts: The Stuttgart Psalter was made around 820–830 at the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés near Paris; its 168 leaves contain the psalms with 316 coloured miniatures set between the verses they illustrate.
Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature.

cur:monumental-castelseprio-pantocrator.summary: In a roundel above the central window of the apse, the bust of Christ, with a golden cross-nimbus, long hair and a gentle oval face, raises his right hand in blessing. Surrounded by the narrative scenes of the infancy cycle, the image gives the whole apse its centre.
facts: The frescoes of Santa Maria foris portas were rediscovered under later plaster only in 1944; their date and the origin of their painter remain controversial, though the first half of the 9th century is increasingly favoured.
They show strong Byzantine influence combined with a freedom of handling recalling late antique painting, and are often described as the finest early medieval pictorial cycle in Italy.
The roundel of Christ sits above the central window; beneath the window are traces of a painted exedra with a Gospel book on a cushion.

cur:objects2-florence-coptic-christ-disc.summary: On this ragged fragment of pale cloth a row of figures is drawn in fine dark outline: a haloed figure, labelled by the museum as Christ, among a group of disciples, one of whom raises an arm. The museum's title associates the scene with Christ and his disciples at the Sea of Tiberias. Even in its damaged state it preserves the delicate linear drawing of Coptic artists of the 6th century.
facts: The Florence archaeological museum holds one of Italy's principal collections of Coptic textiles, formed largely in the 19th century.
cur:objects2-florence-coptic-christ-disc.notes: Title and date are taken from the museum label as transcribed by the photographer; the exact technique (drawn or painted outline on linen) is not stated in the available record, and the scene identification cannot be checked from the image alone.
